But 1418,81-82 sit between 1418,80 and 1418,83, both "Duplicado de carta cifrada de Enrique de Guzmán, conde de Olivares, embajador en Roma" of 17 May 1585, so they are Olivares duplicates whose originals and decipherments would be in the Estado Roma legajos (not checked); and in these Genoa legajos the contemporary decipherment is filed as a separate neighbouring number under a plain "Carta de ..." title (1416,21 is headed "Descifrada" and is the clear text of 1416,22). Each of the eight needs its neighbouring numbers opened and, for 1418,81-82, the Roma legajos of May 1585. Split by item before vetting. 770.unvetted: Not seen, and a clear copy may exist that could not be checked. The Clements finding aid (findingaids.lib.umich.edu, Cloudflare 403 to curl and WebFetch: needs Chrome) is quoted in the entry as "In code [directs Joel Barlow ... to assist Henry Wilson. Wilson will secretly export arms ... from Ostend]": the bracketed summary means the cataloguer had the sense, from a decipherment on or with the letter or from clear passages. The War Department file copy would be in NARA RG 107 letters sent (M6, or the confidential letters M7), not checked; Barlow's 1811 State Department code has an interlinear decipherment at NARA M34 vol. 16. Three web searches (Eustis Barlow 1812 "Henry Wilson" Ostend; Clements War of 1812 collection "In code"; Weber Diplomatic Codes Barlow 1812) found no printed text or study. Needs the 2-page scan from the Clements and a look at RG 107.

Not checked: Livingston to Jay 2 Feb and 27 Apr 1782 (same edition), Livingston to Lafayette 2 Nov 1782 (Idzerda vol. 5), and the notes in the letters near vol. 4 p. 814 and of 5 Sept 1782 in vol. 5. The entry is a list of editorial omissions, not a body of ciphertext.
